skill.name: fetching-library-docs
skill.description: Fetches focused library documentation from Context7, then filters the result into examples, API signatures, overviews, and notes.
skill.summary: Fetch focused Context7 library documentation with token-efficient shell filtering.
skill.author: Asmayaseen

security_audit.summary: The audit confirms a real high-risk subprocess issue in scripts/mcp-client.py because --stdio is executed with shell=True. Most Markdown backtick and reconnaissance matches are false positives, but shell wrappers, unescaped JSON construction, unpinned npx execution, and /tmp PID handling remain reviewable risks.

remediation.issue: Arbitrary stdio command execution in the MCP client
remediation.suggestion: Remove shell=True and accept an argv list, or restrict --stdio to an allowlisted Context7 command.

remediation.issue: Unescaped JSON construction from user-facing parameters
remediation.suggestion: Build MCP parameter payloads with jq or Python json.dumps instead of shell string interpolation.

remediation.issue: Unpinned npx execution for Context7 MCP
remediation.suggestion: Pin @upstash/context7-mcp to a reviewed version and document the expected package source.
Use a private runtime directory, validate PID file ownership, and avoid broad pkill fallback patterns.

semantic_findings.title: Unescaped JSON Parameter Construction
semantic_findings.description: User-derived library, topic, mode, and page values are interpolated into JSON text before calling the MCP client. Quoted shell arguments reduce command injection, but malformed values can alter or break MCP requests.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The files directly build JSON with shell interpolation from user-facing arguments. This is a clear input-safety issue, although not direct shell execution.

semantic_findings.title: Predictable Temporary PID File Controls Process Actions
semantic_findings.description: The start and stop scripts trust a predictable PID file under /tmp. That file can influence process checks and kill operations if it is stale or tampered with.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The scripts visibly use /tmp PID files and then perform kill or pkill actions. The risk depends on local permissions and process ownership, so medium severity is appropriate.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned External MCP Package Execution
semantic_findings.description: The workflow launches @upstash/context7-mcp through npx without a pinned version. A future package change or registry compromise could affect users at runtime.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The command strings show npx -y @upstash/context7-mcp with no version pin. This is a well-defined supply-chain exposure for a runtime dependency.

content.value_statement: Developers need current API examples without filling the chat with long documentation. This skill fetches Context7 docs and returns focused examples, signatures, and notes.
actual_capabilities: Resolves package names to Context7-compatible library IDs.
Fetches documentation by library ID, topic, mode, and page.
Filters documentation into code examples, API signatures, overviews, and notes.
Supports code mode for examples and info mode for concepts.
Shows approximate token savings when verbose mode is enabled.
Includes helper scripts for running a local Context7 MCP server.
limitations: Requires Python, shell tools, npx, and the Context7 MCP package.
Only returns documentation available through Context7.
It is not designed for local repository or source-code exploration.
Filtering can omit details that require more pages or the full docs.
